comments.author: @You-Wish-You-Knew
comments.text: Went from Shanghai to Beijing on high speed train last year. It was so amazing, only complaint is it is hard to get a DD ride from Beijing station, the car park was jam packed

replies.author: @tysoncung
replies.text: Nice, thanks for sharing. Beijing to Shanghai is about 1,300 km, and the fastest trains do it in roughly four and a half hours.

comments.author: @cosmic-minds-origin
comments.text: Worth adding what the two thirds is measured against. China's network passed 48,000 km in 2024 and the next largest, Spain, is around 4,000, so it is not that China leads, it is that China is roughly an order of magnitude ahead of anyone. The oddity is Spain being second at all: a country of 48 million with more high speed track than Japan, which invented it.
